_meta.title: B3 independent gold-topology set
_meta.purpose: Ground-truth circuit topologies for scoring schematic-generation (p300) output, INDEPENDENT of the pipeline. Replaces topology_eval.py's default gold, which is the pipeline's own 4_SG.txt tutorial output on the same 4 prompts (scoring pipeline-vs-self = contamination).
_meta.independence: Every topology below was authored from the prompt's circuit semantics + photonics domain knowledge, NOT copied from any pipeline run. No 4_SG.txt / DSL / CS artifact was consulted for the WIRING. Only the shared PDK vocabulary (component classes + port conventions) is reused — that is the common ontology both arms target, not a pipeline decision.
_meta.what_it_measures: TOPOLOGY correctness only: 'did the schematic wire the right KINDS of components together, with the right connectivity?' Scored node-id-agnostic (typed-edge multiset F1 + component-class F1 + approx_ged, via topology_eval.score_topology). Component SELECTION (which exact cell, e.g. mzi_2x2_pn_diode vs mzi_2x2_heater_tin_cband) is deliberately NOT penalized here — that is A5/B2's job. Both gold and prediction are normalized to component CLASSES (function+arity) via class_map before comparison.
_meta.ambiguity_policy: Each entry carries topology_certain. Prompts that fix the wiring uniquely are true. Prompts that leave the inter-component connection COUNT open (e.g. 'a DC connected to a 2x2 MMI' — one link or a full 2-link cascade?) are false, given a documented canonical reading in 'ambiguity'; these need explicit domain sign-off and may be excluded from the headline F1 or scored with an acceptance band.
_meta.accept: Where more than one component class is functionally correct for a node (e.g. a passive 1x2 power splitter may be an MMI_1x2 or a directional-coupler split), the node lists alternates in 'accept'; the scorer treats any listed class as a typed match for that node.

port_conventions.GC (grating coupler, 1x0): o1 = the single on-chip optical port (the other face couples to fiber/free-space)
port_conventions.1x2 (MMI_1x2, MZI_1x2, PSR, splitters): o1 = single/common side (input), o2 & o3 = split side (outputs)
port_conventions.2x2 (DC_2x2, MMI_2x2, MZI_2x2, coupler_r: o1,o2 = left/input side, o3,o4 = right/output side
port_conventions.RING_2bus (add-drop microring, 2x2): o1 = in (top bus), o2 = through (top bus), o3 = drop (bottom bus), o4 = add (bottom bus)
port_conventions.WDM (wdm_mzi1x4, 1x4): o1 = common/single side, o2..o5 = the four wavelength channels

gold.prompt: A 90 degree waveguide bend
gold.rationale: Single primitive; no internal connectivity. Sanity / component-class check.

gold.prompt: A straight waveguide with a length of 253 um
gold.rationale: Single primitive.

gold.prompt: A ring resonator, single bus, with a radius of 10 microns and a gap of 0.2 microns.
gold.rationale: Single-bus (all-pass) ring is one cell: in + through on one bus.

gold.prompt: A directional coupler, with two inputs and two outputs and 50:50 split ratio
gold.rationale: Single 2x2 coupler.

gold.prompt: A power splitter, with one input and two outputs and 50:50 split ratio
gold.rationale: 1x2 passive 50:50 splitter; canonical is a 1x2 MMI, a 1x2 directional-coupler split is also functionally correct.

gold.prompt: Give me a 2x2 MMI with a gap of 500 nm between the inputs/outputs.
gold.rationale: Single 2x2 MMI.

gold.prompt: A directional coupler connected to a 2x2 MMI.
gold.ambiguity: Canonical reading = full 2-waveguide cascade (both DC outputs into both MMI inputs). A single-link reading (one DC output to one MMI input) is also defensible. Needs sign-off.
gold.rationale: Two 2x2 blocks in series; both right ports of the DC feed the two left ports of the MMI.

gold.prompt: 2 grating couplers connected by a straight waveguide
gold.rationale: GC -- straight -- GC; the two GCs are the fiber I/O, so no on-chip external ports.

gold.prompt: A grating coupler followed by a 1x2 MMI.
gold.rationale: GC into the single (input) port of the 1x2 MMI; two MMI outputs left external.

gold.prompt: A mmi 1x2 followed by a mmi 2x2.
gold.ambiguity: Canonical = both 1x2 outputs into the two 2x2 inputs (2 links). A single-link reading is defensible. Needs sign-off.
gold.rationale: Cascade the 1x2's two outputs into the 2x2's two inputs.

gold.prompt: Connect one output port of a 1x2 MMI to an input of another 1x2 MMI
gold.rationale: Prompt is explicit: exactly one output of MMI-1 to the input of MMI-2 (single link).

gold.prompt: The output ports of an adiabatic directional coupler connected to two straight waveguides
gold.rationale: Both DC output ports each drive one straight waveguide.

gold.prompt: A 2x2 MZI with a phase shifter in each arm for 1 GHz modulation.
gold.rationale: The phase shifters are intra-cell arm elements of an active 2x2 MZI, not separate schematic nodes -> one node.

gold.prompt: Design a 2x2 MZI with two 2 mm long PIN-diodes, one in each arm, for phase modulation.
gold.rationale: Active 2x2 MZI; diodes are intra-cell.

gold.prompt: 2x2 MZI with integrated heaters. the length of the MZI is 500um and the path length difference is 40um
gold.rationale: Thermo-optic 2x2 MZI; heaters intra-cell.

gold.prompt: Create a passive asymmetric Mach-Zehnder Interferometer at 1550 nm with a 300 um path-length difference between arms. The MZI has one input and one output port both terminated in grating couplers.
gold.rationale: 1-in/1-out passive asymmetric MZI, both ports terminated by grating couplers (fiber I/O), so no on-chip external ports.

gold.prompt: Design a single-bus ring resonator (with a radius of 28) connected to two grating couplers for input/output coupling.
gold.rationale: GC -- single-bus ring (in/through) -- GC.

gold.prompt: Connect a 2x2 MZI with integrated thermal heaters to a directional coupler with a length of 125 um, dy of 100 um, and dx of 100 um
gold.ambiguity: Canonical = both MZI outputs into both DC inputs (2 links). Single-link reading defensible. Needs sign-off.
gold.rationale: Two 2x2 blocks in series.

gold.prompt: Design a 1x16 power splitter using 4 stages of 1x2 MMI couplers such that each output port receives an equal share of the input power.
gold.rationale: Balanced binary tree, 4 stages (1+2+4+8 = 15 splitters), 14 inter-stage links, 16 leaf outputs. Fully determined.

gold.prompt: Layout a 1x4 power splitter using three 1x2MMIs. Add 4 thermo-optic phase shifters, one on each output arm, for independent tuning.
gold.rationale: Two-stage 1x4 tree (1+2 MMIs -> 4 outputs); a thermo-optic heater on each of the 4 output arms.

gold.prompt: Cascaded 2x2 MZIs to create a switch tree network with 8 outputs.
gold.ambiguity: 1x8 switch tree = 7 2x2-MZIs (1+2+4), 6 inter-stage links, 8 leaf outputs. Each 2x2 MZI has 2 inputs; the tree uses one input per node (the other is an unused/monitor port) — which input/output indices are used is a layout choice, but the node/edge MULTISET (the scored quantity) is invariant. Marked uncertain only for the unused-port convention.
gold.rationale: Binary switch tree of 2x2 MZIs to 8 outputs.

gold.prompt: Design a 4-channel wavelength demultiplexer using four ring resonators cascaded along a common bus waveguide. Each ring should have a radius of ~10 um, and a 200 nm coupling gap. Provide drop ports for each ring to route the separated channels.
gold.rationale: Add-drop rings serially coupled along one bus: through-port of ring i -> in-port of ring i+1; each ring's drop port is an external channel.

gold.prompt: Connect four amplitude modulators (each 1 in/1 out, >10 GHz electro-optic bandwidth) to a 4x1 wavelength-division multiplexer.
gold.ambiguity: Modulator class: '1-in/1-out >10 GHz amplitude modulator' maps to MOD_1x1 (microring modulator or TW-MZM); acceptable alternates in 'accept'. The 4x1 WDM mux is the wdm_mzi1x4 cell used in reverse (4 channel ports -> 1 common).
gold.rationale: Four 1x1 modulators each feed one channel port of the 4-channel WDM mux.

gold.prompt: Design two cascaded double-bus silicon ring resonators, each with a 10 um radius. In each ring, the top bus is for input/output and the bottom bus is for drop/through ports. The second ring's input bus is connected to the drop port of the first ring, forming a serial filter chain. Each bus-to-ring gap is 200 nm.
gold.rationale: Prompt is explicit: a single link from ring-1's drop port (o3) to ring-2's input (o1).
